data.question: What does the newly recovered Garden City primary aggregate record add to issue #2109, and does it resolve the native charging/docket/disposition chain?
data.method: Compared the City of Garden City September 3, 2024 commission packet containing the July GCPD Master Activity Report with the already-merged #2651 incident records and the contemporaneous May 6 KWCH report attributed to Garden City police.
data.framework: Separate aggregate agency statistics, incident-level attributed reporting, arrest/requested-charge state, filed charges, and adjudicated disposition.
data.scope: Garden City Police public records and directly relevant contemporaneous reporting for the May 4 and July 2024 robbery/arrest sequence already modeled in issue #2109.
findings: The primary July 2024 GCPD report records one robbery offense for July and reports two robbery investigations assigned and one cleared during July, but it is aggregate-only and supplies no suspect name, business name, incident number, complaint number, or court case number.

The official aggregate report therefore corroborates that robbery investigations were active in the relevant month but cannot be used as a deterministic identity join to Alberto Rincon or either named robbery.

The May 6 KWCH report, explicitly attributing its facts to Garden City police, places the May 4 Joyeria America incident at 308 E. Fulton Street and predates any public identification of Rincon in the later arrest coverage.

The 308 E. Fulton wording conflicts with later reporting/issue prose that has rendered the jewelry-store address as 308 W. Fulton; the packet preserves that contradiction rather than silently choosing one.
No native Finney County complaint/information, case number, docket, plea/trial disposition, judgment, or sentence was recovered in this bounded pass.
conclusions: The existing #2651 identity/arrest model remains appropriately limited to police-attributed secondary reporting; the newly recovered city report does not upgrade the legal state to filed charge or conviction.
The native-case target remains necessary and open.
The Joyeria America street-direction discrepancy should remain unresolved until a native incident report, business record, charging instrument, or other primary record resolves it.
recommendations: Recover the Garden City Police incident/arrest report(s) and incident identifiers for May 4, July 1, and July 4.
Recover the Finney County complaint/information and exact case number, then join docket entries to disposition and sentence without inferring convictions from requested charges.
Use the native record to resolve the Joyeria America E/W Fulton address discrepancy.
counterarguments: Aggregate monthly statistics cannot prove that the July robbery rows correspond to the Tacos El Tapatio event or Rincon's arrest; any such one-to-one mapping would be inference.
limitations: The city monthly report is aggregate-only.
Public Kansas court-search surfaces did not yield a deterministic case number in this bounded pass.
The initial KWCH incident article is secondary reporting, although it explicitly attributes facts to Garden City police.
unresolved: Garden City Police native incident/arrest report IDs
Finney County criminal case number and charging instrument
Plea or trial disposition and sentence
Joyeria America 308 E. versus 308 W. Fulton street-direction conflict

findings.finding: Recovered the City of Garden City commission packet containing the July 2024 GCPD Master Activity Report.
The report contains aggregate robbery offense/investigation counts but no Rincon name or case identifier, so it cannot complete the native case join.
The contemporaneous May 6 KWCH report attributed to Garden City police says 308 E. Fulton Street, conflicting with later 308 W. Fulton renderings.
Native Finney County complaint/case/docket/disposition remains unresolved.
